_note: Every household in this file is simulated. Labels stay at the level of 'a retired teacher in Portland' on purpose: no names, addresses or contact details.

households.label: a studio apartment in Tokyo

tips.text: Every hour, stand up for the first minute of a call and roll your shoulders back ten times. It adds up without stealing time.

questions.text: What can I cook in ten minutes after getting home late?

households.label: a retired cook's home in Osaka

tips.phrase: the ten-minute egg and spinach dinner
tips.text: Ten-minute egg and spinach: wilt the spinach in sesame oil, pour in beaten egg with a splash of soy sauce, fold twice and serve on rice.
Stand green onions roots-down in a glass with an inch of water by the window. They keep growing back for weeks.

households.label: a family of four in Seattle

tips.text: Freeze leftover rice in flat portions while it is still warm; it reheats fluffy in two minutes.

tips.phrase: the launch pad basket by the door
tips.text: Keep a launch pad basket by the door. Backpacks, permission slips and keys go in the night before, so mornings start calm.

questions.text: Indoor ideas to keep two kids busy on a rainy Saturday?

households.label: a student in Austin

tips.text: Plan three dinners around one big pot of beans or lentils. It costs a few dollars and freezes well.

questions.text: Small things that help when you feel homesick in a new city?

households.label: a retired teacher living alone in Portland

tips.text: Keep three books on hold at the library. When one arrives, add another, so there is always something waiting.

households.label: a couple who both work from home in Denver

tips.text: Walk around the block before your first meeting and after your last. It marks the start and end of the workday.

households.label: a nurse on night shifts in Chicago

tips.text: Wear sunglasses on the way home after a night shift and keep the bedroom dark and cool. Falling asleep comes easier.

households.label: a single dad with a seven-year-old in Boston

tips.text: Let kids build their own plate from three small bowls. Choosing makes them far more willing to try things.

questions.text: Packed lunch ideas a seven-year-old will actually eat?

households.label: grandparents raising two grandkids in Atlanta

tips.text: Set a timer for twenty minutes of homework, then five minutes of dancing. It keeps everyone going without arguments.

households.label: a retired couple in Phoenix

tips.text: Run errands before 9 a.m. in summer, and keep a frozen damp washcloth for the back of your neck on the way home.

households.label: new parents with a baby in Minneapolis

tips.text: Set up a basket by the bed with water, a snack, burp cloths and a dim light, so night feeds don't wake the whole house.

questions.text: How do you get through the first months of broken sleep?

households.label: a remote worker living alone in Brooklyn

tips.text: Put a standing fifteen-minute call with one friend on the calendar every week. It is easier than finding time each time.

households.label: an engineer sharing a flat in San Francisco

tips.text: Keep a shared grocery list on the fridge with a pen tied to it. Whoever uses the last of something writes it down.

households.label: a musician in Nashville

tips.phrase: leaving the guitar on its stand
tips.text: Leave your instrument out of its case on a stand. You will pick it up far more often than if it is packed away.

households.label: a family with a dog in Raleigh

tips.text: Freeze xylitol-free peanut butter inside a chew toy. It buys a calm half hour while you are on calls.

households.label: a military family in San Diego

tips.text: Pack a first-night box with sheets, towels, chargers, a kettle and snacks. Label it and load it last.

households.label: an office worker caring for a parent in Columbus

tips.text: Keep one notebook for all doctor visits: questions on the left page, answers on the right. Bring it every time.

questions.text: How do other caregivers find a little time for themselves?

households.label: a retired fisherman in Honolulu

tips.text: Pat fish completely dry and salt it ten minutes before cooking. The skin comes out crisp every time.

households.label: a family in Anchorage

tips.text: Turn on a bright lamp at breakfast during the dark months. Mornings feel much less heavy.

households.label: an elderly couple in Kyoto

tips.phrase: letting the water cool for green tea
tips.text: Let boiled water cool for a minute before pouring it over green tea. It tastes sweeter and less bitter.

households.label: a nursery teacher in Fukuoka

tips.text: Turn tidying into a race against one song. Kids love beating the music.

households.label: a single mother of two in Sendai

tips.text: Cook a double batch on Sunday and freeze half in labeled bags laid flat. Weeknight dinners become reheat and serve.

questions.text: Ten-minute ways to recharge when the kids are finally asleep?

households.label: a factory worker living alone in Nagoya

tips.text: Hang shirts on hangers straight from the washer and give each a firm shake. Most won't need ironing.

households.label: a grandmother in Okinawa

tips.text: Do your stretches while the kettle boils every morning. It becomes a habit without needing extra time.

households.label: a couple with a toddler in Yokohama

tips.text: Cut food into shapes with a cookie cutter. Even vegetables disappear faster.

households.label: a university student in Hiroshima

tips.text: Study in 25-minute blocks and write the next small step on a sticky note before every break.

households.label: a retired nurse in London

tips.text: Use a weekly pill box and fill it on the same day each week, right after Sunday breakfast.

households.label: a newcomer family in Toronto

tips.text: Visit the local library first. They often have free classes, events and people who know the neighborhood.

households.label: a long-haul trucker's family in Dallas

tips.text: Read the same book as your kids while you are away and talk about one chapter on each call.

households.label: a retired couple who love dancing in Miami

tips.text: Put on one song and dance through it while dinner cooks. It is the easiest exercise of the day.

households.label: a big family in Salt Lake City

tips.text: Write chores on craft sticks in a jar. Everyone draws two after dinner, and nobody argues about who does what.

households.label: a retired autoworker living alone in Detroit

tips.phrase: taking a photo before taking it apart
tips.text: Take a photo before you unplug or take anything apart. Putting it back together is easy then.

households.label: a pastry chef in Kobe

tips.phrase: setting out eggs while the oven preheats
tips.text: Bring eggs and butter to room temperature by setting them out while the oven preheats.

households.label: a couple with an older dog in Pittsburgh

tips.phrase: the bath mat by the water bowl
tips.text: Put a non-slip bath mat by the water bowl for an older dog. It stops slipping on smooth floors.
